violation_type.title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers-Report Suspected Child Abuse, Neglect or Exploitation (26 TAC §746.1201(5))
violation_type.short_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers-Report Suspected Child Abuse, Neglect or Exploitation
violation_type.typical_finding: Evidence obtained during the investigation confirms staff at the operation had suspicions of children in care being Abused and Neglected outside the daycare and did not make a report to the Texas Department of Family and Protective Services.

finding_variants.text: Evidence obtained during the investigation confirms staff at the operation had suspicions of children in care being Abused and Neglected outside the daycare and did not make a report to the Texas Department of Family and Protective Services.
This standard was tasked as part of an DFPS investigation and found to be deficient. The operation did not report suspected abuse within the required time frame.
During the DFPS investigation, it was found that the director knew about the incident and did not report it to licensing.
This standard was tasked as part of an investigation and found deficient. The center director was made aware of allegations of sexual abuse and failed to report this.

During an investigation it was found that a child had an outcry that a caregiver pulled their ear and this was not reported. I spoke with staff about ensuring that reports are made if there is ever an outcry of abuse.

It was determined throughout the course of the investigation that operational employees failed to report abuse neglect concerns to CPS when they became aware of the situation requiring them to report to the hotline.
